claim: POV decides whose experience the camera, sound and grade are aligned to. Objective watches a character while first_person makes the audience wear him — that is the difference between sympathy and complicity, and it is a choice you make once per scene, not per shot.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: detached observation, neutral level vantage, uninvolved
subjective, character-aligned vantage, shallow focus on him, close emotional proximity
pov, first-person view, viewer's own hands in frame
distant elevated vantage, all-seeing, detached overview
unreliable, warped perspective, doubled image, distorted
shared vantage, over-the-shoulder of another figure, two viewpoints

review.issue: Four of six clauses are prose abstractions with no danbooru equivalent — "detached observation", "uninvolved", "character-aligned vantage", "close emotional proximity", "all-seeing", "two viewpoints" render nothing. objective and subjective will differ only by "shallow focus", and objective vs omniscient only by "elevated". Separately, first_person ("viewer's own hands in frame") and shared ("over-the-shoulder of another figure") both require a second body in frame and so fight "solo, 1boy" in the subject sentence.
review.fix: Use the actual camera tags Animagine knows: objective -> "straight-on, eye level, medium shot"; subjective -> "depth of field, blurry background, close-up"; omniscient -> "from above, wide shot, distant view"; unreliable -> "dutch angle, double exposure, distorted perspective"; first_person -> "pov, pov hands"; shared -> "over the shoulder, from behind, foreground silhouette" and accept that the last two contradict solo (or mark those two options unrenderable under this subject).
